original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: On PR #2979's words (Marius-Paul Dumitrean; unchanged, read in place from main) and, in the registered instance 2979, its allocation: the recursion lever. In #2979's unit, 16,086 of the 28,190 rank-48 blocks (8,064 in child 8, 8,022 in child 10) are literal heads in my lowering and my network: each is the first non-identity operation on its own array, on that array alone, with nothing hosted there before. Cutting each head by 24 of its 48 axes lets its array take a job of 49 axes instead of 73, and a recursion that feeds a word with jobs of two sizes in a fixed ratio (the mixed-target recursion, Theorem 1G of PROOF.md) prices the word at b = 1.7556473153e-3 for the DFT, against #2979's uniform 1.7290339826e-3. The registered check re-derives the heads, the profile and the price from #2979's files and certifies the rate inequality exactly; the DFT bound itself is proved in Lean outside this repository (README section 5). The same check on PR #3945 (second instance, not registered here because its files were on an open pull request when this package was made; archived on main on 20 October 2026 with the same files) gives 57,312 heads and 1.7501109246e-3. On #3945's words with a table of hosts re-solved so that every head is kept (fills/3945H/FILL.json.gz, made by #3815's allocation programs with one added condition; #3945's own complete verification passes on it), instance 3945H gives 80,640 heads and a half-cut price of 1.7581520168e-3, and instance 3945F, the full cut on the same table (the heads removed, job 25 on their arrays; the other 57,312 rank-48 blocks split 24 + 24, so every paid block has rank at most 24 < 25), gives 1.7806935406e-3; the DFT bounds at 1.7581520e-3 and 1.7806935e-3 are proved in Lean outside this repository (README sections 5, 7 and 8). Neither is registered, for the same reason as the second instance. Headline (registered, verify.py --instance 2979Fc, both parts): #2979's words, order and dispatch with a table of hosts re-solved for the full cut (A-fc, fills/2979Fc/); removing its 16,576 literal heads (job 25 on their arrays; no other rank-48 block, so every paid block has rank at most 23 < 25) prices it at b = 1.7887045643e-3, certified at 17887045/10^10; checked by computer, not proved in Lean. Its own uniform figure, 1.6897030e-3, is below #2979's, so the hub's admission rejects it at its strict-gain steps (README section 9).
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed local cost interface beats the current packing within the hub's model. This package does not change the word, the inventory or the packing: it changes the recursion, which is the coverage law. The hub's recursion gives every array the same job; the mixed-target recursion gives the head arrays a job of 49 axes and every other array the full 73. The card's own allowed variation covers this case ('If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope'). The replacement bound is Theorem 1G (PROOF.md), whose hypothesis is that every paid block is smaller than every job (48 < 49); the incumbent ceiling tool assumes uniform jobs and is not applied. The figure is a complex-side b for the DFT in OpenAI's exact-arithmetic machine model; whether the hub's outer step for integer multiplication accepts a supplier with two job sizes is open, so no kappa is claimed.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds (current priorities); the lever adds +1.539 % to #2979's complex root without changing a single gate of its words, and its size grows with the number of literal heads (break-even 1 head for the half cut). On #2979 the half cut lifts b from 1.7290339826e-3 to 1.7556473153e-3, above the selected bit side c = 1.7334270e-3, so if the hub's outer step accepted it the bit side would bind. With a table of hosts re-solved for the full cut on the same words (the headline A-fc, checked by computer, not proved in Lean), b is 1.7887045643e-3, +3.451 % over #2979's root; the highest figure proved in Lean is the full cut on #3945 with every head kept, 1.7806935e-3.
stop_rule: Publish only if the head count in my lowering equals the count from the community's own allocation, the global profile equals PROFILE.json digit for digit, the uniform root reproduces #2979's stated root to 24 digits, the half-cut figure is strictly above every complex-side construction claimed on the hub by others, and the DFT bound at that figure is proved in Lean with the standard axioms and refused one grid step higher. For the headline A-fc the same on its own table and paid profile (the head count from my lowering and from the table, the global profile equal to fills/2979Fc/PROFILE.json, the uniform root equal to the community's root for this table to 24 digits, the full-cut figure strictly above every complex-side construction claimed on the hub by others, its rate certificate at 17887045/10^10 refused one grid step higher), except that its DFT bound is not proved in Lean, which the package states.
evidence: verify.py --part main (standard library): pins; my transport and lowering of both #2979 words (exact replays, residual widths helper by helper, 7 rejected mutants each, recorded content hashes); the head test in my network on all 271,728 FILL rows (16,086 heads, 12,104 other rank-48 blocks, global profile = PROFILE.json, two network controls); the price (uniform root = CLAIM.json complex_lower to 24 digits, half cut 1.7556473153e-3, full cut 1.7744822149e-3 as a what-if); the exact rational rate certificate at 17556473/10^10, refuted at 17556474/10^10. verify.py --part controls: the T74 regression (11,010 heads) and four price controls. Outside this repository (README section 5): the Lean proofs of OpenAI's DFT statement with the exponent 1 - 17556473/10^10 (this instance) and, for the instances below, 1 - 17581520/10^10 (3945H) and 1 - 17806935/10^10 (3945F); the leaderboard's own re-check is of the last one. Second instance: verify.py --instance 3945 on #3945's head files (57,312 heads, 1.7501109246e-3, all controls pass). Headline: verify.py --instance 2979Fc --part main and --part controls (registered): the table and its paid profile pinned by sha256 (fills/2979Fc/FILL.json.gz and PROFILE.json, recorded in instances/2979Fc.json), 16,576 literal heads (8,288 + 8,288) and no other rank-48 block, the global profile equal to fills/2979Fc/PROFILE.json, the uniform root equal to the community's root for this table (1.6897030111e-3) to 24 digits, the full-cut price 1.7887045643e-3, the full-cut profile derived from the measured heads, and the exact rational rate certificate at 17887045/10^10, refused at 17887046/10^10; controls: the figure refused with a single head, with one head fewer, and with the heads kept as blocks of 48 while their arrays take the job of 25. Not in Lean (README section 9). Third and fourth instances: verify.py --instance 3945H (the table pinned by sha256, 80,640 heads, 57,312 other rank-48 blocks, the global profile equal to #3945's, the uniform root equal to its stated root to 24 digits, half cut 1.7581520168e-3, the rate certificate at 17581520/10^10, refused one step higher) and verify.py --instance 3945F (the full cut on the same table, 1.7806935406e-3, the profile derived from the measured heads equal to the Lean rate module Rate3945F, the rate certificate at 17806935/10^10, refused one step higher; controls: the figure refused with a single head, with one head fewer and without the split).

open_questions.question: Does the hub's outer step for integer multiplication accept a complex supplier whose recursion uses two job sizes (73 and 49 axes for the half cut, 73 and 25 for the full cut of the headline) in a fixed ratio?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only then does the complex-side b of this package become a supplier for kappa; until then it is a DFT result in OpenAI's model, compared with the hub's complex side b against b.
open_questions.first_step: Write the mixed-target recursion as a supplier interface in the terms of the outer theorem the hub uses (its recursion, its halving guard m^2 > 2R^2, its portion and rounding steps) and list which hypotheses change; PROOF.md section 3 lists what the mixed recursion needs that the uniform one lacks.
open_questions.blocked_by: A precise statement of the outer theorem's supplier hypotheses for a uniform supplier.

open_questions.question: Is the half cut of the 16,086 heads correct in the hub's own exact eight-stream operator model, not only in my lowering?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The refuted idle-axis moves of 18-19 Oct changed the exact operator while keeping the profile; reviewers will want the cut checked in the hub's own operator model.
open_questions.first_step: Replay the cut of a sample of heads (one per child and replica class) with #3187's exact eight-stream operator replay, as #4046 did for the idle-axis moves, with a control that a wrong cut (24 axes taken from a non-head block) changes the operator.

open_questions.question: Can the full cut on #2979's words (the headline A-fc, checked by computer at 1.7887045643e-3) be proved in Lean?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A-fc is the highest figure here but rests on a computer check of its own instance; the full cut is proved in Lean only on #3945 with every head kept (instance 3945F, 1.7806935e-3). Theorem 1G and the general full-cut theorem are in Lean already.
open_questions.first_step: Build A-fc's instance in Lean the way instance 3945F was built: its heads-first certificate on fills/2979Fc/FILL.json.gz, the cut fact on #2979's words, and a rate module at 17887045/10^10 with the profile of instances/2979Fc.json.

open_questions.question: Beyond keeping every head that the table of hosts allows (done: #3945 with every head kept, README section 7), can more of the rank-48 blocks become literal heads?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The half-cut price rises with every head; on #2979, 12,104 rank-48 blocks (children 12 and 13) are neither heads nor tails, and on #3945 with every head kept 57,312 are.
open_questions.first_step: From the head test's examples (g0 output, 'neither' class), list for each such block the first non-identity touch of its array before its climb, and test whether that touch can be moved after the climb without changing the word's operator.

open_questions.question: Does the lever carry over to the newest staged words (for example #4088 at 1.7309791e-3)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The lever is independent of the word; a word with a higher uniform b and as many heads would give a higher DFT figure.
open_questions.first_step: Write instances/<id>.json for the word (its file paths and sha256) and run verify.py --instance <id>; the expected head count is not known in advance, so start with the head test alone.
open_questions.blocked_by: none: #4088 and the other staged words of that line were archived on main on 20 October 2026; their files can be read there.

open_questions.question: Is the factor (log n)^kappa of Theorem 1G real for grouped paid blocks, or does the mixed recursion reach O(n^tau) exactly?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The DFT figure is unaffected (any saving below the root is reached), but an exact bound would simplify the supplier interface.
open_questions.first_step: Search small separated rules for a flow with Phi(exits) <= (eta - beta) Phi(sources) (PROOF.md, remark after Theorem 1G).
